messages:
jules-devex: FYI a customer reported flaky failures in our JS onboarding sample after upgrading to @redwood/sdk@6.0.0. It only fails in Cloudflare Workers and Bun, works locally in Node. Error they see: 

jules-devex: `Error: The requested module "/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.js" does not provide an export named 'default'`

marta-eng: Do they `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk'` or use named imports?

jules-devex: They use `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'` across several sample files and some helper scripts still expect the default to be a client factory that wires auth+retry middleware. Past releases implicitly provided that via CJS interop.

paul-runtime: This smells like two intertwined regressions: 1) our export map now points import->dist/index.mjs (which no longer exports default), require->dist/index.cjs (CJS still had default), and 2) some bundlers/edge loaders (especially Bun/Workers) strictly follow the import export and don't fall back to CJS so default consumers break. Because some sample tooling transpiles differently per platform, the failure is intermittent across environments.

harper-qa: Also noticed in CI that tsc sometimes complains: `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'` when installing the package tarball. A bunch of TS setups don't resolve conditional `types` in exports and need a top-level "types" field.

marta-eng: Repro steps I used that reproduce the customer issue: 
1) clone onboarding-samples
2) `npm i @redwood/sdk@6.0.0`
3) `wrangler dev` -> immediate default export error

marta-eng: Quick inspection: dist/index.mjs begins with: 

marta-eng: ```js
marta-eng: export * from './client.js';
marta-eng: export { createClient } from './client.js';
marta-eng: ```

marta-eng: No default export. dist/index.cjs still exports `module.exports = require('./client.cjs')` which provides a default-ish shape via CJS interop. The new exports map: 

marta-eng: ```json
marta-eng: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }
marta-eng: ```

paul-runtime: That `types` inside the conditional is still not sufficient for some TS consumers. Also the lack of default in ESM means any code doing `import SDK from` will break on strict ESM platforms.

harper-qa: Besides the runtime break, a deeper problem: some onboarding helpers relied on `@redwood/sdk/legacy` deep import to get an auto-retrying client wrapper. We purposely removed that subpath. We now have users who import the public API expecting the old default client+retry behavior but the new ESM build only exposes the lightweight factories and requires consumers to wire retry/auth themselves. Tests that depended on the old convenience now fail intermittently under load.

jules-devex: Proposed immediate fixes: 
- Add an ESM default shim in dist/index.mjs: `export { createClient as default } from './client.js'` to preserve default-import behavior for one patch cycle.
- Add a top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" in package.json so TS resolves types in more toolchains.
- Reintroduce an explicit public subpath for the old convenience API (e.g., "./legacy": "./dist/legacy.mjs") rather than a wildcard, and mark it deprecated in docs.

paul-runtime: Agreed. Also add a release smoke test matrix that installs the published package and runs: Node (esbuild), Bun, and Workers `wrangler dev` against a minimal sample that does default import, named import, and a deep subpath. That should catch this class of ESM/CJS/export regressions.

harper-qa: I'll add the smoke tests to CI and a tsc check step that installs the tarball and runs `tsc --noEmit` against the sample code. I'll also write a flaky test case that asserts the client still has retry logic when using the legacy convenience import, to prevent silent behavior drift in future releases.

docsy: For customer-facing communication: we should update onboarding samples to prefer `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` and show how to wire retry/auth middleware manually. But we will ship the compat shim and an explicit `./legacy` export for two patch releases, then remove the shim after migration window. Add a short migration note in changelog and an example diff for sample repos.

jules-devex: I've opened a draft PR with the minimal shim + types field + `./legacy` subpath: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1218 (draft). Pinged @marta-eng and @paul-runtime for review.

paul-runtime: Once PR is green, cut 6.0.1 patch and post a note to #general + update onboarding repo. Let's also add an export-map linter to the publish pipeline to catch wildcards or missing types entries in future releases.

harper-qa: Noted. I'll monitor the customer repro and share the workaround (pin to 5.x or switch to named imports) until the patch ships. :thumbsup:
